results.controlIntent: a. Changes to the system are tested before finalizing the implementation of the changes; b. Changes to the system are validated before finalizing the implementation of the changes; and c. Changes to the system are documented before finalizing the implementation of the changes.

judgment.rationale:
Two distinct change-control violations were identified through temporal correlation of CloudTrail events and the model registry entry:

1. **Initial Deployment (CreateEndpoint, 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z):** The CloudTrail record (id: 8a5391ca) carries an explicit annotation stating the endpoint was "Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00." While the raw timestamps show the endpoint was created at 11:00 and approval was at 09:00 (suggesting approval came first), the embedded note flags this as a change-control failure — indicating the deployment sequence or associated testing/validation was not properly completed before the change was finalized.

2. **Hotfix Deployment (UpdateEndpoint, 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z):** The CloudTrail record (id: ec7e2fd5) shows a hotfix config (`churn-predictor-v1-hotfix`) was deployed with "no corresponding registry entry found." The model registry (id: 67b4027e) contains only version 1 with approval dated 2025-12-01 — there is no registry entry for the hotfix. This means the hotfix change was implemented without: (a) a documented model package entry, (b) a formal approval/validation gate, and (c) any evidence of pre-deployment testing. This directly violates all three sub-requirements of CM-3(2).r2: testing, validation, and documentation must precede implementation.

Together, these findings demonstrate that changes to the churn-predictor-endpoint were not consistently tested, validated, or documented before being finalized — the hotfix case being a clear and unambiguous violation.
gaps: No test execution records (e.g., SageMaker Experiments, CI/CD pipeline logs) were available to confirm pre-deployment testing for any change.
No change request tickets or approval workflows (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow) were available to corroborate documented change authorization.
The hotfix registry entry (churn-predictor-v1-hotfix) is entirely absent — human attestation would be needed to determine whether any out-of-band approval occurred.
Additional CloudTrail history prior to 2025-11-30 would help establish whether the initial model creation followed a proper change process.
